newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW-Independent targets Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Independent targets Asia.

text.p: Irish-based newspaper, media and advertising group Independent Newspapers Plc said on Wednesday it was targeting Asia for growth over the next few years.

Independent Newspapers' chairman, Heinz chief Tony O'Reilly, said his flagship Irish company has now become a truly global media group and was well positioned to achieve further profitable growth in 1997.
Independent reported a 47 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit to 73.5 million Irish pounds ($115 million) on turnover of 419 million pounds, up from 368 million pounds in 1995.
The media company's chief executive, Liam Healy, said Independent's balance sheet was healthy and he saw Asia as its next major target for expansion.

"Our strategy is to continue to develop within the media. We see development out of Australia and New Zealand into Asia," Healy told Reuters in an interview. "We have started Buspak (outdoor advertising) in Hong Kong and we intend to bring that down through Asia over the next few years."
He said Independent was also looking at magazine and specialist publishing in Asia through Singapore and Hong Kong out of either Australia and/or New Zealand.

"We find Asia looks very promising and we are quite confident of considerable development in different sections in Asia," Healy said, adding that the group would look for a local partner in its ventures where, he said, countries were only opening up in terms of technology, publishing and advertising.
Healy said Independent had a healthy balance sheet and the group could comfortably spend another 200-300 million Irish pounds on acquisitions if the right opportunities came along.
"We are very pleased with the result and the growth of the company. We are now as big as the Mirror Group Plc in Britain," Healy said.
He said 25 percent of the growth in 1996 could be attributed to organic growth which was led by the 33 percent rise in operating profits out of Ireland.
In 1997 he expected New Zealand, where the group now owns almost 86 percent of publishing house Wilson & Horton Ltd, to become the star performer.
"The driver in 1996 was Ireland and that was due to the buoyant economy and the buoyant advertising which was up 18 percent (industry wide) and we were a little better than that," Healy said.
He said advertising demand in Ireland in 1997 has remained very buoyant and he saw that buoyancy continuing for some time.

Healy said in 1997 he expects roughly 45 percent of earnings to come from New Zealand where Wilson & Horton reported a rise of six percent in operating profits to NZ83.3 million (35.8 million Irish pounds) in the 1996 results.

Britain, where the group undertook a rationalisation programme in 1995, also did well, Healy said. "Regional papers did well and our magazines had their best year to date and seem to be continuing on that trend."

He said he expected Australia, which had a number of lean years, to pick up in 1997 while in South Africa, where the group holds a 60 percent stake in Independent Newspapers Holdings, the focus will now turn to radio.

"We are involved with partners in applying for radio licenses in South Africa. We have gone into radio in a big way in Australia and New Zealand and we will go the same route in South Africa and Asia," Healy said.
